source_name: Radio Prague International (english.radio.cz)
why_relevant: Czech Radio's public-service English service; reliably translates domestic economic and consumer-finance stories (cash usage, bank fees, currency) for an international audience. Secondary but well-attributed English restatement of CZ facts.

source_name: Kurzy.cz RSS — Czech economic news and rubric feeds
why_relevant: Broad Czech economic-news aggregator with per-rubric RSS (investment, personal finance, business) that syndicates bank and ČNB items; a low-cost always-on monitoring layer that also mirrors registry and company data.

source_name: ČNB RSS channels (cnb.cz/cs/obecne/rss)
why_relevant: Publisher-side feed layer of the central bank: notifies on new statistical releases, methodological notices and registry changes. The cheapest way to detect when a payment-statistics series is republished, restructured or withdrawn — the trigger for an archival capture.

source_name: ČNB 'Archiv' sections (retired supervisory and market summaries)
why_relevant: The publisher's own archival layer holding superseded aggregate financial-market summaries and official notices — the first place to look for discontinued series before falling back to web archives.

source_name: Emerging Europe / The Fintech Times — regional English re-publication of CZ payments and fintech developments
why_relevant: Regional English outlets that periodically profile the Czech payments/fintech landscape and aggregate CZ numbers into CEE comparisons; useful for benchmarking framing, weak as a data source (figures are usually recycled from ČNB/vendor reports).

source_name: Český statistický úřad (ČSÚ) — Czech Statistical Office, main portal
why_relevant: National statistical authority and the root pointer for all CZ official statistics outside the central bank: retail turnover, household expenditure, ICT/e-payment behaviour, business ICT and e-commerce. Domain migrated from czso.cz to csu.gov.cz, so both hostnames must be tracked.

source_name: ČSÚ — Otevřená data (open data landing page / LKOD)
why_relevant: Entry point to ČSÚ's Local Open Data Catalogue (LKOD), listing machine-readable statistical datasets, code lists and classifications that feed the National Open Data Catalogue. This is the main pointer to further machine-readable series relevant to retail, ICT and household payment behaviour.

source_name: ČSÚ DataStat — statistical data application and public API
why_relevant: DataStat exposes ČSÚ time series (including short-term trade / retail turnover statistics) through a documented REST API returning JSON-STAT. This is the highest-value machine-readable route to CZ retail and consumption series that contextualise card/cash spend.

source_name: ČSÚ Veřejná databáze (VDB) — public statistical database
why_relevant: The long-standing multidimensional query database for all published CZ statistics — retail turnover, household expenditure, ICT indicators. Useful for back-series that DataStat may not expose. JSF-based UI makes scraping brittle; prefer its export endpoints.

source_name: ČSÚ — ICT v domácnostech a uživatelé ICT (household ICT survey, incl. internet banking & online payments)
why_relevant: The Eurostat-harmonised annual household ICT survey is the authoritative non-central-bank source on internet banking penetration, online purchasing and online payment behaviour by age/region — the demand-side complement to ČNB payment statistics. Example finding: internet banking used by 77% of persons 16+ in 2024.

source_name: ČSÚ — Podniky a ICT / Využívání ICT v podnikatelském sektoru (business ICT & e-commerce survey, ICT 5-01)
why_relevant: Annual ICT 5-01 survey of enterprises covers e-commerce sales, web sales channels and the financial significance of e-commerce transactions — the merchant/acceptance side that frames POS and e-commerce acquiring demand in CZ.

source_name: ČSÚ — Information Society in Figures (English annual publication)
why_relevant: English-language annual compendium of CZ vs EU digital indicators including internet banking, online shopping and web sales — the fastest route to comparable figures without Czech-language parsing.

source_name: ČSÚ — Statistika rodinných účtů (SRÚ, household budget survey linked to SILC)
why_relevant: The household-diary survey (~3,000 households, continuous since 2017, linked to Životní podmínky/EU-SILC) records daily monetary expenditure by category — the only official CZ micro-level basis for consumer spending structure that underpins cash-versus-card usage analysis.

source_name: ČSÚ — Krátkodobé statistiky obchodu / Maloobchod (short-term retail turnover, Rychlé informace)
why_relevant: Monthly retail turnover releases are the standard denominator for card-spend and POS-volume analysis (turnover growth, e-shop segment split). Published on a fixed calendar as 'Rychlé informace' with machine-readable annexes.

source_name: Statistika&My — ČSÚ analytical magazine
why_relevant: ČSÚ's own commentary channel: interprets ICT/digital-society and consumption releases, flags upcoming survey rounds, and often surfaces indicators before they are easy to find in the databases. Good early-warning and pointer layer.

source_name: NKOD integration documentation & reference LKOD implementation (datagov-cz on GitHub)
why_relevant: Documents the exact machine interfaces (SPARQL, TPF, GraphQL) and DCAT-AP profile used by NKOD, plus the reference local-catalogue implementation. Essential to build a durable harvester rather than scraping the portal UI.

source_name: Portál otevřených dat Ministerstva financí (data.mf.gov.cz)
why_relevant: MF ČR's own open-data portal with 1,100+ datasets covering the ministry and its subordinate bodies (tax and customs administration, public budgets, control activity), and its own SPARQL catalogue endpoint. Includes an EET (electronic sales records) topic area directly relevant to POS/cash-register policy.

source_name: MF ČR — Otevřená data: publikační plán a výroční zpráva
why_relevant: The ministry's annual open-data report and publication plan announce which datasets will be opened next — a forward-looking pointer letting the intelligence programme anticipate new machine-readable financial-sector series rather than discover them late.

source_name: MF ČR — Zpráva o vývoji finančního trhu (annual financial market development report)
why_relevant: The ministry's flagship annual report quantifies household financial assets by product including cash holdings ('nebo držený v hotovosti'), bank deposits and market structure, and narrates national and EU legislative change affecting payments. Directly relevant to cash-usage and market-sizing workstreams; back-issues available from ~2014.

source_name: MF ČR / financnigramotnost.gov.cz — Měření úrovně finanční gramotnosti
why_relevant: Quinquennial nationally representative survey (>1,000 respondents, 100+ questions; latest wave January 2025) run by MF with ČNB and fed into the OECD/INFE international comparison. Covers household budgeting, payment discipline, product holding and consumer behaviour — a rare official behavioural source outside the central bank.

source_name: Finanční správa ČR — EET / EET 2.0 programme pages and technical documentation
source_subtype: tax authority programme / technical spec publisher
why_relevant: The tax administration is re-launching electronic sales records (EET 2.0), publishing technical guidelines for POS/cash-register vendors, a test environment and DIS+ integration timelines. This is a first-order regulatory driver for POS terminal and cash-register demand in CZ and a source of aggregate transaction-reporting statistics.

source_name: Portál statistik MPO (Ministry of Industry and Trade statistics portal)
why_relevant: Launched June 2024, publishes time series of financial indicators for non-financial enterprises and trade-sector aggregates (employment, revenue, commercial margins in wholesale/retail). Provides the merchant-economics context for POS acceptance and interchange discussions. English mirror exists.

source_name: Státní pokladna (MF ČR) — MONITOR / state treasury payment accounts and cards pages
why_relevant: Operational documentation of how state organisations use payment accounts and ČNB-issued payment cards. Indirect but reveals public-sector card issuance/acceptance arrangements and procurement-adjacent detail, and MONITOR exposes public-budget data as open data.

source_name: ČTÚ Open Data (Czech Telecommunication Office open data portal)
why_relevant: Sector regulator open-data portal surfaced while searching NKOD-linked publishers. Relevant indirectly: mobile/broadband penetration and postal-services data condition mobile payment, e-commerce delivery and cash-on-delivery behaviour; also a template for how CZ regulators expose LKOD datasets.

source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) – Statistiky
why_relevant: The single most important non-regulator source of Czech card-market statistics: quarterly and annual series (2000-present, plus a historical file back to 1989) covering number and value of cashless transactions at merchants, ATM withdrawals, cashback at retail, e-commerce card transactions, and cards in circulation. Data are aggregated from the card issuers/acquirers themselves (Česká spořitelna, ČSOB, KB, mBank, Raiffeisenbank) and the schemes (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Diners, JCB, Discover), i.e. exactly the granularity individual banks will not release.

source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty – O SBK / statut a členská základna
why_relevant: Enumerates the card-industry actor landscape in CZ: reportedly ~18 regular members (issuers/acquirers) and ~23 observers (processors, schemes, terminal vendors, service providers). This is the fastest way to build a complete list of every organisation touching cards, POS acquiring and ATM operations in the country.

source_name: Česká bankovní asociace (ČBA) – Členové
why_relevant: Authoritative roster of ~31-35 banks, building societies and foreign bank branches representing ~99% of the Czech banking sector. Turns one page into a near-complete map of the CZ banking actor landscape (Air Bank, Česká spořitelna, KB, ČSOB group, mBank, MONETA, Raiffeisenbank, UniCredit, plus BNP Paribas, Citibank, Deutsche Bank, HSBC, ING branches).

source_name: ČBA Monitor – banking sector and macro indicator portal
why_relevant: ČBA's dedicated data portal with six recurring indicator families: Ekonomika, Bankovní sektor (assets, employment, profitability, capital adequacy, interest income), Úvěry a vklady (credit/deposit dynamics, NPL ratios, rates), ČBA Hypomonitor (mortgage volumes and rates), Ceny nemovitostí, ČBA Prognóza. Gives association-curated aggregates and commentary, updated monthly/quarterly.
